questions.question: How should the Azure range-reader read-after-close bug be handled?

options.label: Fix now via bug protocol (Recommended)
options.description: New BUG backlog item, CHANGELOG entry, failing test first, then the fix: raise ValueError like a standard file object. Also check seek() and tell() after close. One PR on a fix branch.

options.label: Backlog item only
options.description: Record it as a BUG item with the reproduction and fix it later. Nothing else changes now.

options.label: Leave it
options.description: It's an internal reader and the store layer may never call it after close, so the misleading error doesn't matter in practice.

questions.question: Should Pyright become part of the repo's checks?

options.label: No, local tool only (Recommended)
options.description: mypy strict stays the only type check. Pyright stays an on-demand local check plus the editor plugin. No new CI job or noise to maintain.

options.label: Pyright default checks, non-blocking
options.description: Add a [tool.pyright] config that silences the false positives above, plus a job that reports results without failing the build. Worth it only if you expect it to catch things mypy misses.

options.label: Pyright default checks, blocking
options.description: Same config, plus the 'unbound' and Protocol cleanups, and the job must pass. Most rigorous, but two type checkers to keep happy on every change.

questions.question: Do the cosmetic cleanups as well?

options.label: Skip them (Recommended)
options.description: None of them changes behaviour. Touching about 30 files for annotation style creates churn and merge conflicts.

options.label: Annotations only
options.description: Change Iterator to Generator on the 31 context managers and accept None for size in the two read() methods. Mechanical, low risk.

options.label: All of it
options.description: Annotations, plus restructure the memory-backend listing so the variables are obviously set, plus explicit __all__ lists.

questions.question: How wide should BUG-310 go?

options.label: Conformance test, all backends (Recommended)
options.description: Add a spec clause (read/readinto/seek/tell on a closed stream raise ValueError) and a conformance test over read() and read_seekable() for every backend, using real backends not fakes. Fix whatever fails: at least the two Azure adapters, maybe HTTP. Effort M. Matches the 'rock solid' goal.

options.label: Both Azure adapters
options.description: Fix _AzureRangeReader and _AzureBinaryIO with Azure-only unit tests. No spec change. Effort S. The HTTP adapters stay unverified.

options.label: Range reader only
options.description: Only what Pyright found. Effort S. Leaves the silent b'' on Azure read() in place.

questions.question: What about the S3 prototype's _S3RangeReader, which has the identical bug?

options.label: Fix it alongside (Recommended)
options.description: Same few lines and the same test. It's excluded from the package, but whoever revives the prototype then inherits correct code.

options.label: Leave it
options.description: The prototype is parked and not shipped. Mention it in the backlog entry only.

questions.question: The branch is 1 commit behind origin/master (BUG-309, #1090). Rebase before opening the PR?

options.label: Rebase and force-push (Recommended)
options.description: git rebase origin/master, then push --force-with-lease. The branch is new and unpushed, so nobody else tracks it. Gates then run against current master; BUG-309 touches tooling, so a conflict in BACKLOG.md is unlikely but possible.

options.label: Open the PR without rebasing
options.description: Push as is. GitHub may show the branch out of date, and the backlog ID-set gate compares against a master that has moved on.

options.label: No trace: filing only (Recommended)
options.description: CLAUDE.md requires a trace when an item is implemented, and the trace is opened when implementation begins. Filing-only PRs like BK-409 (#1080) and BK-408 (#1076) shipped none. The PR body states why.

options.label: Open a trace now
options.description: Create sdd/traces/bug-310-closed-stream-read.yml with the reads done so far (spec 036, spec 006, _stream.py, the probes), so the person who implements it starts from them.

questions.question: The review fix surfaced a separate defect. tell() (and seek()) on Azure's non-seekable read() stream raise RemoteStoreError('seek') even while the stream is open, because _ErrorMappingStream maps io.UnsupportedOperation, which is an OSError subclass. Plain Python file objects raise io.UnsupportedOperation. What should happen with it?

options.label: File as its own item in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: Mint BUG-311 under § 2 with the measurement, and leave BUG-310's dossier pointing to it. A different diagnosis (open stream, any non-seekable backend wrapped by _ErrorMappingStream) and a different fix (let UnsupportedOperation through), but the same wrapper, so each item names the other.

options.label: Fold into BUG-310
options.description: Widen BUG-310 to 'stream errors that aren't backend failures get mapped'. One fix touches _ErrorMappingStream for both. The item stops being only about closed streams.

options.label: Leave it in the dossier note
options.description: No item. It stays recorded as an out-of-scope observation in BUG-310's dossier.
